# <span id="aanchor151"></span> Inventory Editor

Use the Inventory Editor to create, edit, and delete gas <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">inventory locations<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Inventory locations, such as underground sotrage caverns, are used to track storage amounts. An initial amount is added to or subtracted from the inventory. The results can then be viewed and reported in FLOWCAL.</span></a>.

The Inventory Editor has two primary tabs: Flow Data and Configuration. The Flow Data tab lists all Inventory Periodic records. The Configuration tab contains details and configuration options for injection and withdrawal points, characteristics, and site information.

Inventories can be viewed in the Meter/Location Rollups Viewer.

<div class="procedure">

To create a new inventory location:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**.

2.  Click the **New Inventory** button or go to **Inventory** \> **New**.

3.  Enter an inventory location number.

4.  Enter an inventory name (optional).

5.  Select an injection point and/or withdrawal point (station locations). Entering at least on of these location points is required. If the items you need are not in the menu, you will need to add them through the [Location Editor](../Location%20Editor/Location%20Editor.md).

6.  Click the **Characteristics** tab to edit the status.

7.  Click the **Edit Status** button to change the status. Options are "Active", "Inactive", "Long Term Monitoring", and "Plugged and Abandoned".

    If the status is set to "Inactive", "Long Term Monitoring", or "Plugged and Abandoned", exceptions will be generated if the inventory changes during that time period.

8.  Complete the applicable information on the Site tab.

9.  Click the **Save** button.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 513;height: 275;" />

</div>

The following options are available on the Inventory Editor screen:

- **Inventory Location Number** - A unique identifier that the user sets for the inventory location. This field is required to create the inventory location.
- **Inventory Location Name** - Optional field to identify a name for the inventory location.
- **Flow Data/Configuration** - Select whether to view the location by all flow data for the Inventory or by the inventory's configuration setup
- **Injection Point** - An existing station location set as an inlet that acts as the injection point for gas coming into the inventory location.
- **Withdrawal Point** - An existing station location set as an outlet that acts as the withdrawal point for gas leaving from the inventory location.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Periodic Record">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Periodic Records</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Periodic Record">

Set the inventory to a specific value using an inventory periodic record.

<div class="procedure">

To create an inventory periodic record:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**.
2.  Go to **Periodic** \> **New**.
3.  If the inventory location is a liquid type, enter the gross standard volume, net standard volume, and/or mass. If the inventory location is a gas type, enter volume, energy and/or mass.
4.  Select a date and hour.
5.  Click the **Save** button.

To edit or delete a periodic record, select a row, and click **Periodic** \> **Edit** or **Periodic** \> **Delete**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Validations">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Validations</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Validations">

FLOWCAL can validate specified volume or mass quantities against user-defined limits.

<div class="procedure">

To view the Inventory Validations screen:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**.
2.  Select a gas inventory.
3.  Go to **Tools** \> **Validations**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 245;height: 175;" />

</div>

The following options are available on the Validations screen:

- **Total Volume/Mass** - Select volume or mass as the quantity to track, and specify the total quantity amount the inventory can hold. If the FLOWCAL-calculated inventory amount for any given hour exceeds this amount, an exception will be generated.
- **Max/Min Fill** - If the FLOWCAL-calculated inventory amount exceeds or falls below the percentage of the total quantity amount, an exception will be generated. This provides a warning to users when nearing the bottom or nearing the overfill limit for the inventory.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Info">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Info</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Info">

Details about the inventory contents are available in the Inventory Info screen.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Inventory Info screen:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**.
2.  Select a gas inventory.
3.  Go to **Tools** \> **Info**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 466;height: 397;" />

</div>

The following options are available on the Inventory Info screen:

- **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a gas inventory is always "Gas".
- **Requires Close Approval** - Gas inventories that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in [Location Close Approval](../Close%20Approval/Close%20Approval.md).

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Tools">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Tools</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Tools">

The Inventory Tools screen provides access to several inventory configuration options:

- **Contact Selections** - Contacts can be assigned to a gas inventory. These will allow for notification for messages and exceptions.
- **Show Tools** - When this option is enabled, the menu icons at the top of the inventory editor are displayed. When it is not checked, the menu icons are hidden.
- **Validations** - FLOWCAL will validate either volume or mass, against a user-defined limit.
- **Info** - User can configure FYI information and import options for the inventory.

</div>
